successors.name: Nabataean Kingdom
successors.text: 5th century BC: Qedar 'controlled the Negev and northern Sinai, reaching the eastern Nile Delta' and 'dominated the northern Hejaz' (page); Al Jawf, Tabuk, the Negev and North Sinai (231,000 km2) is…

ledger.x: 853 BC (first dated king): Gindibu leads 1,000 camelry at Qarqar.
738 BC: Zabibe pays tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III; the Neo-Assyrian dossier has the Mu'na Arabs paying tribute after 734 but not Qedar.
716 BC: Samsi gives Sargon II gifts.
652 BC: Abiyate and Yuwaite back Shamash-shum-ukin's revolt; Yauta had already rebelled in 671 and 669 and been imprisoned, and Sennacherib had captured Dumat in 691.
539 BC: Qedar enters the Achaemenid Empire.
343 BC: Artaxerxes III 'may have ended Qedar's political independence'.
343 BC: the expanded lands go back to the Persian satrapies (bridged with the line above).
343 BC (bridged): Qedar ends as a kingdom; the Qedarites are assimilated by the Nabataeans 'at the end of the Hellenistic period'.

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar (Qedar's camelry)
wars.outcome: Gindibu of Qedar led 1,000 camelry in the coalition of Aram-Damascus and Israel against Shalmaneser III at Qarqar in 853 BC.

wars.name: Samsi's revolt and Tiglath-Pileser III's campaign
wars.outcome: Samsi pledged allegiance after the 734 campaign and rebelled in 733; the Assyrian king attacked Qedar at Mount Saqurri and forced her to flee to Wadi Sirhan; she later paid 125 white camels.

wars.name: Sennacherib's campaign against Qedar
wars.outcome: Sennacherib campaigned against Qedar and captured Dumat in 691 BC, during the reigns of Te'elhunu and Haza'il; Hazael then paid tribute until Sennacherib's death and visited Nineveh in 681.

wars.name: Yauta's revolts against Esarhaddon
wars.outcome: Yauta rebelled during Esarhaddon's Egypt campaign in 671 BC and was defeated; he returned in 669, rebelled again and was later imprisoned by Ashurbanipal (undated).

wars.name: Ashurbanipal's campaign against Qedar and Nabataea
wars.outcome: The Qedarites backed Shamash-shum-ukin's revolt in 652 BC; Ashurbanipal's three-month campaign in 645 BC captured Abiyate while Yuwaite fled.

wars.name: Nabonidus against the Qedarites and Dadan
wars.outcome: Nabonidus defeated the Qedarites, who had backed Dadan, before Cyrus; the Neo-Babylonian dossier has him take Tayma c.

certainty.note: The page names the Wadi Sirhan, the Jauf and later the Negev, Sinai and northern Hejaz but no frontier; the shapes are provincial readings.
